ca-commit.stops: No commit on a red suite, no wildcard staging, no protected-branch commit. “Looks good” is not permission. A stale acceptance blocks before staging.
ca-commit.produces: A local commit, its explicit paths and a gate report. Not a push or PR by itself.
route: You ask for a commit, or run {{commit}}.
Phase 1, permission: an explicit instruction is on record. “Looks good” is not one.
Phase 2, branch: never the protected default branch.
Phase 3, classification: one commit type and scope. Mixed changes are split.
Phase 4, verification: focused tests, lint and a secrets scan of every staged file.
Phase 5, behavioral proof: current output proves the acceptance criterion.
Phase 6, diff review: no unexpected files, secrets, stubs, skipped tests or scope creep.
Phase 7, selective stage: every path is named. Wildcards are blocked (H-03).
Phases 8 and 9: a Conventional Commits message, then the local commit.
ca-commit.simple: The nine-step commit gate before a change is saved to history: permission, branch, tests, proof, review and more. Any step can stop it.

ca-pr.tagline: Open or finish a pull request, watch CI, clean up.
ca-pr.what: {{pr}} opens a pull request once the current-head commit and acceptance check out, runs the applicable diff reviewers and clears blockers. {{pr --watch}} attaches a hosted-CI watcher that diagnoses red and offers the merge on green. {{pr --cleanup}} finishes a merged branch with proof of containment and consent per item. A merge happens only when you select it, hosted CI is green on the exact head and ADR source ancestry checks out.
ca-pr.machine: The shipping dock, with a crane that only you can release.
ca-pr.stops: Never writes to the default branch directly. No inferred merge or discard authority.
ca-pr.produces: An open PR, and optionally an explicitly authorized merge.
route: Creation checks the current-head commit and acceptance.
The applicable reviewers challenge the exact diff.
Blocking findings are resolved before the PR advances.
The PR opens and hosted CI runs on the exact head. {{pr --watch}} diagnoses red.
Merge only if you select it, with green exact-head CI and verified ADR source ancestry.
The change reaches the default branch by pull request, never by direct push.
ca-pr.simple: Packages the change for review as a pull request, watches the shared tests and merges only when you say so.

ca-release.tagline: Prepare a release; publish only with authority.
ca-release.what: {{release}} resolves the declared target and version policy, prepares the version bump and changelog through the ordinary commit gate on a non-default branch, opens the release PR and stops. Only after that PR merges may a qualifying hosted publisher compose the tag and publish from the exact verified default-branch commit, then read the published release back. {{release --dry-run}} only reports.
ca-release.machine: A launch gantry with a hold-down clamp. The clamp is the release PR stop.
ca-release.stops: A mandatory stop at the release PR. No local tag fallback, no publishing a red or stale head, no implicit consent. CI success alone is not publication permission.
ca-release.produces: A release-preparation PR, then a separately authorized publication and its readback.
route: You run {{release}} when release authority is explicit. {{release --dry-run}} only reports.
The declared target, version policy and payload are resolved.
The version bump and changelog go through the ordinary commit gate on a non-default branch.
The release PR opens and the lane stops. No local tag is made.
After the PR merges, a qualifying hosted publisher works from the exact verified commit.
Publication needs its own authority. CI success alone is not permission.
The published release is read back against the declared inventory.
ca-release.simple: Prepares a new version of the software and stops for review. Publishing happens later, and only with explicit permission.

ca-review.tagline: Run the reviewer fleet over the current diff.
ca-review.what: {{review}} selects reviewers by the actual paths in the diff, gives each one its own bounded context, runs them as independent read-only units and funnels their reports through triage into one verdict. CRITICAL and HIGH findings block the current change.
ca-review.machine: An inspection gantry spanning the line.
ca-review.stops: A prediction or a missing result cannot stand in for a completed review. Missing critical context blocks a substantive verdict.
ca-review.produces: A triaged verdict with blocking findings separated from the rest.
route: You run {{review}} on the current diff or a path.
Reviewers are selected by the actual diff paths.
Each reviewer gets its own bounded context and runs as an independent read-only unit.
Findings are classified by severity and by whether they block this change.
A CRITICAL or HIGH finding blocks the change until it is resolved.
ca-review.simple: Calls in the relevant inspectors for the current changes and gives one verdict. Serious problems block.

ca-checkpoint.what: {{checkpoint}} runs the reviewer fleet across the whole codebase, adds the architecture-drift reviewer to compare the code with accepted ADRs, triages the findings and writes a dated, non-overwriting report to `.codearbiter/checkpoints/`. It is informational, not a promotion or merge gate.
ca-checkpoint.machine: A radar dish that sweeps the whole floor.
route: You run {{checkpoint}}, optionally with a focus.
The fleet runs, plus the architecture-drift reviewer comparing code with accepted ADRs.
Findings are triaged into one verdict.
A dated report is written to `.codearbiter/checkpoints/`. It is informational, not a merge gate.
ca-checkpoint.simple: A periodic health check of the whole codebase, saved as a dated report.

ca-threat-model.tagline: An opt-in STRIDE pass for a sensitive design.
ca-threat-model.what: {{threat-model}} runs a lightweight STRIDE analysis (spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, elevation of privilege) over a sensitive design’s assets and trust boundaries, and returns threats and mitigations to the design owner. It is opt-in, never a routine change gate.
ca-threat-model.machine: A shield with six facets, one per STRIDE category.
ca-threat-model.stops: A critical unmitigated threat stops the pass.
ca-threat-model.produces: A threat and mitigation analysis that constrains the design.
route: You run {{threat-model}} for a sensitive design.
Assets, trust boundaries and `security-controls.md` frame the analysis.
A lightweight STRIDE pass runs with the applicable specialists.
Threats and mitigations return to the design owner as constraints.
ca-threat-model.simple: An optional security brainstorm for a sensitive design: how could someone attack this, and what stops them?

ca-tribunal.tagline: A deep, resumable, multi-lens audit. Never a routine gate.
ca-tribunal.what: {{tribunal}} is a deliberate deep audit. It estimates cost from a deterministic inventory and waits for your acknowledgement before any model is dispatched. Each applicable lens card (thirteen ship today, from appsec to typesafety) runs as a read-only reviewer, at most five at once, and findings persist immediately so an interrupted run can resume. Serious claims get an independent verify pass. Issue filing and telemetry each need separate approval.
ca-tribunal.machine: A ring of lenses turning around one subject.
ca-tribunal.stops: Cost acknowledgement before dispatch. Never a commit or merge gate. No automatic repair, ADR or task write.
ca-tribunal.produces: A source-bound audit run and report.
route: You deliberately ask for a deep audit with {{tribunal}}.
Scope and evidence are bound to the current source. A matching unfinished run can resume.
A cost estimate is shown. Nothing is dispatched until you acknowledge it.
Each applicable lens runs as a read-only reviewer, at most five at once. Findings persist immediately.
Serious claims get a fresh, independent verify pass.
The report is written. Issue filing and telemetry each need their own approval.
ca-tribunal.simple: A deep, expensive audit through many lenses at once. It shows the cost first and never blocks routine work.

ca-adr.tagline: Record a numbered, user-attributed architecture decision.
ca-adr.what: {{adr}} writes an Architecture Decision Record. It reads the current decision context, presents the decision and its alternatives, takes your explicit choice and attribution, and writes the numbered ADR. While authoring it holds a fresh marker that lets the write gate admit the file; at any other time, writes to `decisions/` are blocked (H-11). Accepted ADRs are immutable.
ca-adr.machine: An engraving station. Only this station holds the stylus.
ca-adr.stops: A `[CONFIRM-NN]` answer is never guessed. Accepted or planned is not evidence of delivery.
route: The current decision context, related ADRs and open questions are read.
The decision and its alternatives are presented. You choose, and the choice is attributed to you.
The lane holds a fresh authoring marker, so the write gate admits the ADR (H-11).
A numbered, dated ADR is written. Once accepted, it is immutable.
ca-adr.simple: Writes down an architecture decision with your name on it, so the why is never lost.

ca-adr-status.what: {{adr-status}} reads the ADRs and reports their age, challenges and supersession chains. It grants no writing authority and is not evidence of delivery.
ca-adr-status.machine: An archive reader with a magnifier.
route: Status mode is selected before any authoring step.
Age, challenges and supersession chains are reported. Nothing is written.
ca-adr-status.simple: Reads the decision records and reports on their health, without changing anything.

ca-reconcile.tagline: Resolve architectural variance with explicit, attributed choices.
ca-reconcile.what: {{reconcile}} compares architectural records (plans, the decision log, ADRs) with the code. Restricted scouts gather cited evidence, the grader produces a SMARTS comparison and an optional decision-challenger red-teams it. You select the ruling. Report-only mode writes nothing; reconciliation mode appends only your attributed choice to the decision log.
ca-reconcile.machine: A balance scale with the SMARTS prism at its pivot.
ca-reconcile.stops: The grader recommends and never decides. Contradictory governing rules go to the conflict protocol instead.
ca-reconcile.produces: A variance report, or an attributed architectural ruling.
route: You run {{reconcile}}, optionally with a scope.
Report-only or reconciliation mode is chosen.
Restricted scouts gather cited evidence as paths and line numbers.
The grader produces a SMARTS comparison; an optional challenger red-teams it.
You select the ruling. The grader recommends; it never decides.
In reconciliation mode, your attributed choice is appended to the decision log.
ca-reconcile.simple: When the code and the recorded decisions drift apart, it lays out the evidence and the options so you can rule.

ca-conflict.tagline: Stop everything and surface both sides.
ca-conflict.what: When governing rules, documents and code contradict each other, the conflict protocol stops other work, presents both sides with the conflict hierarchy and waits for you. It is an internal protocol: the orchestrator invokes it, and you rarely type it. When it is unclear whether to reconcile or stop, it stops.
ca-conflict.machine: The red emergency stop. It halts the line until you clear it.
ca-conflict.produces: A visible stopped state and a specific decision request.
route: Governing rules, documents or code contradict each other.
Both sides are shown with the conflict hierarchy and the exact evidence.
You decide. Nothing is reconciled silently.
ca-conflict.simple: The emergency stop. When the rules themselves contradict each other, everything halts until you decide.

ca-status.tagline: Read project state; inspect provenance drift.
ca-status.what: {{status}} shows the project’s live state and changes nothing. {{status drift}} compares governed documents with their recorded provenance and reports each as current, stale or unknown. A refresh happens only for documents you explicitly select, and it never stages or commits.
ca-status.machine: A panel of gauges that reads the record.
ca-status.produces: A read-only state or drift report.
route: The default path reads live project state and changes nothing.
Drift compares each governed document with its provenance: current, stale or unknown.
A refresh happens only for documents you select. It never stages or commits.
ca-status.simple: A dashboard of the project’s current state. It only reads.

ca-task.tagline: Add, start and finish tasks through the only sanctioned writer.
ca-task.what: {{task}} changes the task board through one sanctioned writer, which validates every transition. start stamps a date, done requires the task to be in progress, and a task is never deleted to complete it. A debug result alone never writes a task; a follow-up needs its own authority.
ca-task.machine: A kanban board with a single pen.
ca-task.produces: A task entry or a valid state transition.
route: You run {{task add}}, {{task start}} or {{task done}}.
The transition is validated by the only sanctioned writer, under an OS lock.
start stamps a date; done requires in progress; nothing is deleted to complete it.
ca-task.simple: Adds, starts and finishes tasks on the board through the one approved pen.

ca-doctor.tagline: Prove the install is actually enforcing.
ca-doctor.what: {{doctor}} verifies the active install: interpreter, payload version, package ownership, hook wiring, and a harmless live-fire probe that triggers a real H-03 block. It reports capability gaps. Run it after installing, after updating and whenever a gate seems to be missing.
ca-doctor.machine: A probe that fires one harmless test charge into the shell gate.
ca-doctor.stops: A healthy report does not prove that any lane completed.
ca-doctor.produces: An installation and enforcement diagnostic report.
route: You run {{doctor}} after install, or when a gate seems missing.
Interpreter, payload, package ownership and hook wiring are inspected.
A harmless live-fire probe triggers a real H-03 block. Seeing it block is the proof.
ca-doctor.simple: Checks that the guards are really installed and working, by setting one off harmlessly.

ca-override.tagline: One logged, attributed bypass where a rule permits it.
ca-override.what: {{override}} is the sanctioned exception. The reason must name the gate and justify the bypass; a vague reason is rejected. A routine gate takes one confirmation and one attributed line in `overrides.log`. Security-critical stops (a CRITICAL security finding, the crypto and secret commit gates, irreversible operations) take a heavier path: the finding stated verbatim and your acknowledgement of that specific finding, logged as a security override.
ca-override.machine: A key switch wired to the audit tape. Every turn prints a line.
ca-override.stops: Not universal bypass authority. The raw-secret prohibition has no exception in any mode.
ca-override.produces: An attributed audit line and a bounded continuation.
route: You run {{override}} with a specific reason naming the gate.
The governing rule must permit a bypass. A vague reason is rejected.
Routine gates take one confirmation. Security-critical stops need the finding stated verbatim and your acknowledgement of it.
One line is appended to `overrides.log`: time, your email, the gate and the reason.
Work proceeds only within that boundary. The statusline counts overrides since the last checkpoint.
ca-override.simple: A signed exception. Where a rule allows it, you can bypass a gate once, and your name and reason go into the permanent log.

ca-standup.tagline: Repository hygiene, confirmed one action at a time.
ca-standup.what: {{standup}} inspects branches, worktrees, stashes and the working tree, reports unsafe or ambiguous residue and offers safe cleanups. You confirm each one separately; only fast-forward and permitted cleanups run. A read-only version runs as the first-of-day briefing at session start.
ca-standup.machine: A morning bell beside a clipboard.
ca-standup.stops: Dirty, stashed or unpushed work is never silently discarded.
ca-standup.produces: A hygiene briefing and individually authorized cleanup results.
route: You run {{standup}}, or accept the offer from the daily briefing.
Branches, worktrees, stashes and the working tree are inspected.
Unsafe or ambiguous residue is reported, never silently discarded.
Each cleanup is confirmed separately. Only fast-forward and permitted cleanups run.
ca-standup.simple: A morning tidy-up: finds old branches and leftovers and asks before cleaning up each one.

ca-audit.what: {{audit}} reads the source governance records for a window (overrides, triage, decisions, checkpoints) and assembles a dated, non-overwriting evidence packet. It quotes audit lines exactly and changes nothing at the source.
ca-audit.machine: A records press that binds pages into a packet.
route: You run {{audit}}, optionally with a range.
The source governance records for the window are read.
A dated packet is assembled. Existing packets and source records are never overwritten.
ca-audit.simple: Gathers the governance records for a period into one dated evidence packet.

ca-statusline.tagline: A Claude Code statusline with a governance row.
ca-statusline.what: {{statusline}} installs, removes or reports the optional Claude Code statusline: folder, git state, rate limits, token use, cost, context headroom, model and session age, plus a governance row in enabled repositories. It backs up and restores any previous statusline. Claude Code only.
ca-statusline.machine: The LED strip along the edge of the ring.
ca-statusline.produces: Statusline configuration or a status report.
route: You run {{statusline install}} in Claude Code.
A ca-owned statusline entry is installed, backing up any previous one.
In enabled repositories a governance row appears. Session start keeps the path current after updates.
ca-statusline.simple: A status bar for Claude Code that shows usage, cost and the governance state at a glance.

ca-prune.args: status | dry | run <path> | audit <path> | on | off
ca-prune.tagline: Trim transcript bulk. Live pruning is a preview.
ca-prune.what: {{prune}} inspects or trims redundant transcript content so long sessions last longer before compaction. Dry-run is the default. On Claude Code it never rewrites the live transcript; gains apply after resume or compaction. Pi uses its native compaction instead. Live pruning is an opt-in Feature Forge preview enabled with `CODEARBITER_PRUNE`.
ca-prune.machine: A compactor beside the press, painted preview orange.
ca-prune.produces: A report, or reduced transcript bulk after resume or compaction.
route: Live pruning is an opt-in preview. Dry-run is the default.
Redundant transcript bulk is identified. On Claude Code the live transcript is never rewritten.
Savings apply after resume or compaction. Pi uses native compaction instead.
ca-prune.simple: Finds redundant content in long session transcripts so sessions last longer before compaction. It only reports unless you opt in to the preview.
